query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve dynamic strength–ductility performance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an untreated baseline, defines the boundary conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

evidence_appraisal.reason: Some principles may apply to high-entropy alloys

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a specific phase transformation, such as FCC-BCC, can improve dynamic strength-ductility performance in high-entropy alloys.
generation.intervention: Introduction of a specific phase transformation
generation.mechanism: Derived from materials-science principles, supported by record node::10.1016/j.ijplas.2023.103730
generation.boundary: High-entropy alloys with specific compositions and processing histories
generation.uncertainty: Dependence on specific alloy composition and processing route

falsification_experiment.design: Dynamic loading experiment with high-entropy alloy samples
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no improvement in strength-ductility performance is observed, the hypothesis is falsified
